questions.stem: What does Bill Inmon's 3NF Data Modelling approach build?
options: A centralised Enterprise Data Warehouse in normalised, typically Third Normal Form, structure
A set of independent star-schema data marts built first for analytics
A key–value cache of loan records
An append-only event log
A graph of customers and officers
questions.explanation: Inmon's approach organises enterprise data in a normalised structure, typically 3NF, to build a centralised Enterprise Data Warehouse that serves as the single source of truth.

questions.stem: Which four characteristics describe the Inmon Enterprise Data Warehouse?
options: Denormalised, fast, intuitive and process-oriented
Subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant and non-volatile
Schema-less, distributed, partitioned and eventually consistent
Immutable, append-only, replayable and streaming
Hierarchical, navigational, rigid and pointer-based
questions.explanation: The EDW is subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant and non-volatile, serving as the authoritative single source of truth for the organisation.

questions.stem: What does a 3NF Enterprise Data Warehouse prioritise over direct query performance?
options: Horizontal scalability
Developer productivity
Data quality, traceability and long-term governance
Minimal table count
Real-time responsiveness
questions.explanation: The 3NF EDW prioritises data quality, traceability and long-term governance, defining core entities once and integrating them across source systems.

questions.stem: How is Customer data from a CRM system and from a Core Banking system handled in an Inmon-style EDW?
options: Each system's customer records are stored in separate warehouses
Only the CRM version is loaded
They are stored as duplicate rows for traceability
They are reconciled and integrated under a single enterprise identifier
They are embedded together in one JSON document
questions.explanation: Data from operational systems is extracted, cleansed, standardised and integrated, so customer data from CRM and Core Banking is reconciled under a single enterprise identifier.

questions.stem: How are business intelligence queries typically served in the Inmon architecture?
options: Directly from the normalised EDW tables
From a key–value cache in front of the EDW
From the operational source systems
From a graph database layered on the EDW
From dimensional data marts derived from the EDW, such as star or snowflake schemas
questions.explanation: The 3NF EDW is not optimised for direct BI queries, so dimensional data marts are derived from it to serve reporting and dashboard needs.

questions.stem: What metaphor describes the relationship between the Inmon EDW and downstream data marts?
options: Hub and spokes: the EDW is the hub and marts are spokes tailored for analytical use cases
Parent and child: each mart owns part of the EDW
Producer and consumer: marts emit events to the EDW
Client and server: the EDW queries the marts
Key and value: the EDW is the key and marts are values
questions.explanation: In this design the EDW acts as the hub and the downstream data marts act as spokes tailored for specific analytical use cases.

questions.stem: In the Inmon-style loan approval EDW, which table has OfficerID and BranchID where BranchID is a foreign key?
options: Loan
Officer
Approval
Branch
Status
questions.explanation: The Officer table has OfficerID as primary key and BranchID as a foreign key referencing the Branch table, with one row per officer.

questions.stem: In the 3NF loan approval EDW, what does one row of the Approval table represent?
options: One customer
One loan account
One approval decision event
One branch
One status value
questions.explanation: Approval (ApprovalID PK, LoanID FK, OfficerID FK, StatusID FK) holds one row per approval decision event.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a trade-off of 3NF Data Modelling in an EDW?
options: Designing and maintaining the EDW can be complex and time-consuming
Query performance for end users may be slower unless marts are created
The model is less intuitive for business users than a star schema
Every data element loses traceability to its source
Analytical queries may require multiple joins
questions.explanation: Traceability is a strength of the 3NF EDW: every data element can be traced back to an integrated, controlled source, which supports regulatory requirements.

questions.stem: How does Inmon's philosophy contrast with Kimball's approach?
options: Inmon builds star schemas first; Kimball builds a normalised core first
Inmon uses NoSQL; Kimball uses relational databases
Inmon rejects data marts entirely; Kimball rejects the warehouse
Inmon is real-time; Kimball is batch
Inmon is EDW-first, building the normalised core then deriving marts; Kimball is dimensional-first, building marts directly for analytics
questions.explanation: Kimball's dimensional-first approach builds data marts directly for analytics and integrates them conceptually later, while Inmon builds the normalised enterprise core first and derives marts as needed.
